name: Longi Hi-MO 5 500W
notes: Technology: monocrystalline cells (no stated architecture beyond generation-era mono), 132 half-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass. Runs 500-510W. Pros: high Voc (45.55-45.85V) suits shorter series strings, and it's a mature, dependable platform for larger arrays. Cons: no bifacial option, and it trails newer TOPCon/HPBC panels on temperature coefficient and rear-side yield.

name: Longi Hi-MO 5m 410W
notes: Technology: monocrystalline half-cell (6x18 layout), monofacial with single 3.2mm tempered glass. A single 410W entry. Pros: a smaller-format alternative to the full Hi-MO 5 for roofs that can't take a 132-cell module. Cons: notably steep -0.34%/°C Voc temperature coefficient - the coldest-sensitive Voc figure in this database - so cold-climate string lengths need extra care; lowest efficiency (21%) of LONGi's panels here.

name: Longi Hi-MO 6 430W
notes: Technology: HPBC (hybrid passivated back contact) cells, 108 half-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass. A single 430W entry point for LONGi's zero-busbar back-contact line. Pros: HPBC's flatter -0.23%/°C Voc coefficient outperforms PERC-era panels in heat, with a fully black, busbar-free face. Cons: monofacial only despite the premium back-contact technology, and it's the base bin below the higher-power Hi-MO 6 Scientists variants.

name: Longi Hi-MO 6 Scientists 440W
notes: Technology: HPBC (hybrid passivated back contact) cells, 108 half-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass. Runs 440-450W. Pros: all three bins share HPBC's flatter -0.23%/°C Voc coefficient, and the 450W top bin maximises yield in a standard footprint with a clean, busbar-free look. Cons: monofacial only - LONGi doesn't offer a bifacial HPBC variant in this range - so there's no rear-side gain even on a favourable mounting.

name: Longi Hi-MO X6 Max Artist 505W
notes: Technology: monocrystalline cells, 120-cell large-format layout, monofacial with single 3.2mm tempered glass. A single 505W entry. Pros: the highest-wattage standard-footprint panel LONGi offers in this database, useful where roof space is the binding constraint. Cons: no stated cell architecture and no bifacial option, so despite the flagship wattage it doesn't carry the temperature/degradation advantages of LONGi's HPBC panels.

name: Longi Longi Hi-MO X10 Artist 475W
notes: Technology: monocrystalline cells, monofacial with single 3.2mm tempered glass. A single 475W entry. Pros: the gentlest Voc temperature coefficient in this entire database (-0.20%/°C), which widens cold-string headroom more than any other panel here. Cons: that flat coefficient comes with a higher Isc (15.03A) than most 475W-class modules, so check controller current limits; no bifacial option.

name: LONGi Hi-MO 7 595W
notes: Technology: N-Type TOPCon cells (LONGi's HPDC variant), half-cell, 132-cell (6x22), bifacial with dual 2.0mm+2.0mm glass. Runs 595-625W - a large-format utility/commercial panel, not a standard residential module. Pros: bifacial gain (80%+-5%) on top of a 12-year product / 30-year linear power warranty (87.4% of nominal power at year 30), and UK trade pricing is unusually competitive for an N-type bifacial glass-glass panel at roughly PS60-85 ex-VAT per panel. Cons: at 2382mm long and 33.5kg it needs a roof, tray, or ground mount built for large-format modules - it will not fit standard residential in-roof or rail systems sized for smaller panels; Isc approaches 16A, so check MPPT current headroom on wide parallel strings.

name: LONGi Hi-MO 9 635W
notes: Technology: N-Type HPBC 2.0 (back-contact, 'BC-CELL') cells, 132-cell (6x22), bifacial with dual 2.0mm+2.0mm glass. Runs 635-670W and is LONGi's utility-scale flagship, one step above Hi-MO 7. Pros: the highest module efficiency in this database (up to 24.8%), a flatter temperature coefficient than Hi-MO 7 (-0.26%/degC vs -0.28%/degC), and the same 12-year product / 30-year linear power warranty. Cons: this is a utility/large-commercial product - at 2382mm and 32.7kg it needs the same large-format mounting as Hi-MO 7, and UK residential trade stock and per-unit pricing are far less established than the smaller Hi-MO 7 or the residential-focused Hi-MO S10, so treat it as commercial-project-only for now.

name: LONGi Hi-MO S10 490W
notes: Technology: HIBC cells (LONGi's back-contact cells combined with HJT-style passivation), 108-cell (6x18), bifacial with dual 2.0mm+1.6mm semi-tempered glass. Runs 490-505W and is LONGi's current flagship residential panel, positioned above Hi-MO 6/X6. Pros: the highest efficiency residential panel in this database (up to 24.7%) with a 30-year product AND 30-year linear performance warranty - longer cover than any other panel here bar Maxeon's 40-year term - plus anti-shading cell electronics and a Class A fire rating. Cons: at 1800mm it is taller than most standard-footprint residential panels (verify roof/tray fit), and as LONGi's newest 2026 flagship, UK stock is still building relative to the well-established Hi-MO 6 range.
